modules.summary: Native Swift implementation of Anthropic Messages API request construction, Claude model detection, system prompt cache splitting, URL normalization, authenticated HTTP requests with retries, OpenAI-compatible JSON response conversion, token usage mapping, and incremental Anthropic SSE-to-OpenAI SSE conversion.

Native Swift implementation of the centralized LLM HTTP transport, including chat endpoint normalization, DeepSeek V4 model detection, OpenAI-compatible response parsing, configurable request retries and timeouts, bearer authentication, extra request-body overrides, token usage extraction, and injectable telemetry and API-key validation. Uses Foundation, URLSession, Codable-compatible JSON values, async/await, and typed errors without introducing application-specific dependencies.

Native Swift implementation of the centralized non-streaming LLM gateway, including task-based routing, configurable requests through LLMTransport, JSON-mode system prompting, legacy configuration-based calls, deterministic SHA-256 request fingerprints, and concurrency-safe in-flight request deduplication with shared results and errors.

Native Swift conversation persistence subsystem with a unified store API, configurable write-disable gate, branching story JSON persistence, safe conversation identifiers, active-path window retrieval, atomic story document updates, and isolated SQLite private-chat storage with schema migration and message CRUD. The core implementation is provided as multiple reusable Swift files. Full compatibility remains partial because the private-chat implementation does not yet cover every legacy migration and query helper in the Python source.
next_steps: Complete private-chat compatibility by adding appendAssistantParts with injectable clock and broadcast callback, and verify all result payloads against the Python contract.
Review legacy database migration edge cases, including column defaults, concurrent initialization, SQLite error propagation, and rollback behavior.
Add compatibility support for every exposed private storage helper and verify persona/audio migration failure handling.
Integrate against the existing project’s SQLite3 module configuration and confirm deployment-platform availability without adding tests or changing unrelated modules.
capabilities: Defines chat and private persistence channels and a unified SaveStore protocol with channel-based factory selection.
Implements a concurrency-safe write-disable gate with process-level override and SAVE_DISABLED environment-variable support.
Resolves configurable storage roots without embedding machine-specific paths.
Validates story conversation IDs and confines JSON paths to the configured saves root.
Loads story documents with compatibility handling for valid JSON followed by trailing content.
Traverses active story paths with cycle protection and supports bounded window retrieval, parent/sibling inclusion, root variants, and legacy flat-document fallback.
Writes full story documents using atomic temporary-file replacement and supports incremental message upserts, deletions, and metadata patches.
Creates the isolated private_chat directory structure and SQLite schema, adding missing legacy columns idempotently.
Migrates a legacy private_chat.db and legacy persona files when possible, and supports optional migration of referenced audio files.

Implements private message insertion with client-ID idempotency, injectable sticker validation, windowed pagination, deletion, recall, field updates, image lookup, recent-role retrieval, dialog-row retrieval, and user-message retrieval.
Provides typed Swift errors and result models, Foundation-based Codable serialization, SQLite3 access, and dependency-injected storage configuration.
Documents source mapping, public APIs, persistence behavior, configuration, migration assumptions, and usage.

modules.summary: Native Swift companion-research subsystem combining heuristic search-intent detection, provider-aware web and Xiaohongshu search, normalized results, conversational context synthesis, MCP status and feed handling, and guarded image downloading. Uses Foundation, URLSession, async/await, injectable LLM closures, and filesystem and URL-validation boundaries.
capabilities: Implements skip-search and fast-intent heuristics, source-bias scoring, search-mode resolution, JSON intent parsing, and prompt construction.
Implements provider-independent web search using optional Serper, Wikipedia, DuckDuckGo Instant Answer and Lite fallbacks, plus Xiaohongshu search.
Normalizes and deduplicates heterogeneous search results and formats prompt-ready summaries.
Supports Xiaohongshu MCP configuration, bearer authentication, health and login status, feed normalization, and image-candidate selection with image-note preference.
Orchestrates intent classification, multiple queries, result digestion, context-block formatting, and structured metadata.
Supports optional LLM intent and digest closures without hardcoding a specific LLM gateway API.
Implements feature-flagged image search, injected SSRF validation and image-type detection, bounded downloads, unique filenames, and persistent image output.
Uses injectable HTTP transport, configuration, LLM calls, URL safety validation, image-type detection, and storage dependencies.
Includes request timeouts, HTTP status validation, response-size limits, URL scheme checks, typed errors, and graceful provider fallbacks.
Documents source mapping, configuration, APIs, architecture, limitations, and usage.

modules.summary: Implemented a cohesive, reusable native Swift MusicBackend subsystem covering playlist persistence, default playlist seeding, safe playlist identifiers, session persistence, NetEase Cloud Music API configuration, song search and normalization, play URL fallback, song details, playlist details, and typed errors. The implementation preserves unknown JSON fields and unrecognized track payloads where possible, injects storage and HTTP dependencies for reuse, and documents the public API. No tests, builds, or git operations were run.
capabilities: Persist playlists as playlist_<id>.json files, enumerate them in sorted order, ignore malformed playlist files, and seed defaults when no valid playlists exist.
Sanitize playlist identifiers using the source-compatible ASCII identifier rules, cap identifiers at 48 characters, and generate fallback IDs when needed.
Preserve arbitrary playlist fields and raw track JSON while supplying default playlist names and track URL/cover fields during writes.
Persist the music session in _session.json, return an idle session when the file is missing or invalid, and preserve arbitrary session keys.
Generate idle session payloads with the expected playback, playlist, invite, position, and millisecond timestamp fields.
Configure the NetEase API base URL and cookie from environment variables, validate HTTP(S) base URLs, and expose a status object without exposing cookie contents.
Perform asynchronous HTTP GET requests with the NetEase Music referer, timeout configuration, query-parameter cookie handling, and typed transport and HTTP errors.
Search songs and normalize song IDs, titles, artists, albums, cover URLs, and duration values.
Resolve playable song URLs using the high-quality endpoint followed by the unblock fallback, returning a meaningful error when no URL is available.
Fetch normalized song details and playlist details with playlist metadata and normalized tracks.
Provide an aggregate MusicBackend facade and a README describing subsystem boundaries, behavior, and integration.

modules.summary: Migrates the character daily-schedule service into a cohesive, reusable Swift subsystem. Preserves the dictionary-based JSON contract while implementing default templates, file persistence, date and time utilities, sleep-aware block filtering, runtime state resolution, persona and inspiration prompt construction, asynchronous LLM generation, tolerant response parsing, template fallback, and the complete resolve-today workflow.
capabilities: Provides the default schedule template, Chinese prompt instructions, weekday and weekend selection, and compatibility with existing JSON keys.
Normalizes date strings using the source-compatible YYYY-MM-DD pattern and supports injectable date and calendar context for deterministic scheduling.
Converts HH:MM values to minutes and back, finds the active schedule block, handles midnight-spanning intervals, and computes sleep overlap.
Filters schedule blocks that overlap configured sleep windows and resolves awake, pre-sleep, sleeping, and gap runtime states.
Loads and saves templates, daily schedule files, and runtime state using Foundation JSONSerialization, preserving additional JSON fields where practical.
Builds generation prompts using template blocks, gap notes, lifestyle context, persona excerpts, sleep settings, and optional web-search inspiration.
Supports asynchronous, injected LLM and inspiration-search closures without inventing provider APIs or credentials.
Parses fenced or embedded JSON responses, validates and normalizes blocks, sorts generated blocks, and falls back to template schedules when generation fails or returns invalid data.
Reuses existing daily schedules unless forced to regenerate, respects disabled templates, persists resolved state, and builds the prompt block for downstream character conversations.
Documents the public API, dependency injection, persistence layout, compatibility decisions, and integration example.

modules.summary: A reusable native Swift migration of cloud/services/mailbox.py. The subsystem provides JSON-backed postcard persistence, index maintenance and recovery, inbox/outbox/unread filtering, read-state mutation, user and AI postcard creation, AI response normalization, prompt construction, and recent postcard context injection. Storage is isolated behind an actor and a configurable directory URL. The implementation preserves the source module's JSON field names, tone normalization, ID validation, text limits, sorting, and default behavior.
capabilities: Represent JSON values and postcard records without tying the subsystem to a web framework.
Persist postcard records as individual JSON files and maintain a capped, newest-first _index.json.
Read cards defensively and rebuild the index from valid card files when recovery is required.
Create user and AI postcards with source-compatible defaults, trimming, validation, and read-state behavior.
List all cards, inbox cards, outbox cards, and unread AI cards with Python-compatible negative-limit slicing semantics.
Count unread cards, mark one card read, and mark all currently indexed unread inbox cards read.
Normalize AI-generated subject, body/content, sticker, cover tone, and reply target fields.
Build reply and proactive postcard prompts, including bounded recent-dialog and optional sticker context.
Inject recent AI postcard context into chat prompts.
Expose the source cover-tone options in their original order and normalize invalid tones to warm.
Use injectable clock and ID generation for deterministic integration and caller-controlled runtime behavior.

modules.summary: Maintains a cohesive Foundation-based Swift port of the behavior-routing backend. Refines compatibility around Python-style truthiness, numeric confidence coercion, mode normalization, prompt construction, JSON parsing, and result metadata while retaining the established public API and injected asynchronous LLM boundary.
capabilities: Implements all four route identifiers and six cue labels with typed Swift enums.
Preserves deterministic hard-exit and hard-enter patterns, evaluation order, confidence values, and case-insensitive matching.
Implements NSFW acknowledgement and aftercare classification plus the short daily-message fast path.
Preserves source behavior for standalone heuristic calls with unnormalized mode strings and normalizes mode at the full-pipeline boundary.
Builds the Chinese system prompt and user prompt, truncating recent dialogue to the last 1,800 Unicode code points.
Parses direct, fenced, and embedded JSON responses without exposing malformed-response errors to callers.
Normalizes unknown route and cue values and implements Python-like truthiness fallback for empty strings, null, false, zero, and empty JSON containers.
Converts numeric JSON values, booleans, and numeric strings to confidence values, then applies source-compatible 0...1 clamping behavior, including non-finite numeric strings.
Provides asynchronous dependency injection for LLM execution, preserving fast-path avoidance and the expected success/error metadata shapes.
Provides a JSON-compatible dictionary representation for callers that need the source's original result shape.
Documents public APIs, integration responsibilities, compatibility behavior, and known runtime differences.
Keeps implementation limited to the selected backend source and does not introduce frontend code, credentials, tests, builds, or Git operations.

modules.summary: Reusable Foundation-only Swift implementation of the debug trace persistence subsystem. Preserves recent and pinned trace semantics, JSON compatibility, sanitization, timestamp normalization to Beijing time, usage normalization and estimation, usage backfilling, patching, deletion, and pin promotion. Storage location, clock, and identifier generation are injectable for integration flexibility.
capabilities: Loads and persists recent and pinned trace collections from a JSON file, tolerating missing, malformed, or structurally invalid persisted data.
Keeps the five newest unpinned recent traces and maintains pinned traces without a retention limit.
Appends and updates traces by identifier while preserving existing raw output and recall metadata when omitted from an update.
Pins recent traces, promotes supplied traces to pinned storage, and updates existing pinned traces without duplicating identifiers.
Deletes traces from both collections and patches only the supported fields.
Sanitizes trace identifiers, timestamps, slot, model, user input, system prompt, raw output, recalls, usage details, and usage source.
Normalizes timestamps with timezone offsets to Beijing time and formats timestamps to second precision.
Normalizes usage-token aliases, cache-token counts, and thinking-token metadata while retaining compatible JSON values.
Estimates usage with model-specific character-to-token ratios and a separate heuristic for reasoning and thinking models.
Backfills usage through an optional token-counting closure, falling back to calibrated estimates when counting fails or yields no result.
Uses actor isolation for serialized operations within one service instance and atomic Foundation file writes for persisted updates.
Exposes Codable JSON values and typed Swift models so callers can integrate the subsystem without relying on untyped JSON dictionaries.

modules.summary: A cohesive, reusable Swift diary subsystem that ports the supplied Python diary service: date normalization, tolerant entry reading and writing, preservation of unknown JSON fields and arbitrary tag values, day summaries, reverse-chronological index listing, monthly calendars, reflection prompt construction, and reflection-result application. The implementation keeps filesystem access injectable, exposes typed models and explicit errors, and avoids dependencies on unrelated subsystems.
capabilities: Normalize date strings using the source service's YYYY-MM-DD shape check and injected current-date provider.
Create default diary entries with matching user, AI, timestamp, sticker, and tag fields.
Read diary JSON files, fall back to empty entries for missing or invalid files, and merge known fields while preserving unknown fields.
Write UTF-8 JSON with two-space indentation and unescaped Unicode, creating parent directories as needed.
Generate compact and full day summaries with trimmed content, sticker values, content-presence flags, and 40-character user previews.
List diary JSON files in descending filename order, applying the requested limit before date-stem validation and producing source-compatible fallback summaries for malformed entries.
Generate month calendars with a full summary for every day in the requested month.
Expose the original Chinese reflection and scheduled-reflection system prompts.
Build reflection prompts from the entry, the last 2,000 Unicode scalar values of recent dialogue, and an optional sticker instruction block.
Apply reflection results using toUser/to_user fallback semantics, trimmed private content and sticker handling, millisecond timestamps, and optional scheduledAt updates.
Preserve arbitrary JSON values, unknown entry and section fields, and non-array tag values instead of silently coercing them.
Use a configurable filesystem root, calendar, timezone, and current-date provider for reuse in app and server contexts.

modules.summary: Ports the moment-thumbnail backend into a reusable native Swift service. It preserves the original cache directory and naming conventions, reuses existing JPEG/JPEG/PNG thumbnails, selects deterministic gradients using MD5, resolves emoji code points and caches Twemoji downloads, creates standards-compliant PNG files without third-party dependencies, supports recent-moment batch maintenance, and provides an injectable image-processing boundary with an Apple ImageIO/CoreGraphics implementation. Where native image processing is unavailable, the fallback preserves the source module's behavior of copying original images or saving an emoji PNG or generated gradient PNG.
capabilities: Provides typed moment inputs, ready-thumbnail results, configuration, protocols, and typed errors.
Creates the 缩略图 and _emoji_cache directories under a caller-configured moments directory.
Constructs stable, sanitized thumbnail filenames and looks for existing .jpg, .jpeg, and .png files in source-compatible priority order.
Uses an MD5 digest of the moment identifier to select the original twelve deterministic gradient palettes.
Converts emoji to lowercase hexadecimal Unicode code points while omitting variation selector U+FE0F.
Fetches version-pinned Twemoji PNG resources using an injectable asynchronous HTTP client, a bounded request timeout, and a persistent disk cache.
Implements PNG signature, IHDR, IDAT, and IEND chunks, CRC-32 checksums, zlib framing, Adler-32 checksums, and uncompressed DEFLATE blocks using Foundation and Swift standard-language operations.
Generates 256-by-256 RGB gradient PNG backgrounds without relying on Pillow or another third-party package.
Supports injectable image processing and includes an ImageIO/CoreGraphics processor for square center-cropped JPEG thumbnails and gradient-plus-emoji composition on supported Apple platforms.
Uses the first valid user-image source in moment order before falling back to emoji or text-background generation.
Preserves the original distinction between processed JPEG output and fallback PNG or copied-original output.
Supports forced regeneration, cached-result reuse, recent-moment limits, per-moment failure isolation, and ready results containing moment identifiers and filenames.
Uses actor isolation for service operations and atomic file writes for generated assets.
Documents source mapping, APIs, configuration, fallback behavior, and integration limitations.

modules.summary: 将 should_send_voice.py 的自动语音决策逻辑整理为独立、可复用的原生 Swift 子系统。保留快速拒绝规则、提示词构造、LLM JSON 解析、置信度阈值、错误安全回退和 meta 标记；LLM 调用通过异步注入闭包完成，不绑定具体供应商或重复实现传输层。修正 JSON 解析边界：只有 JSON 解码失败时才尝试从文本中提取对象；有效但非对象的 JSON 会作为解析异常交由服务层统一返回 llm-error。
capabilities: 提供可配置的语音决策服务、结构化结果模型、元数据模型及解析错误类型。
复刻空文本、多段内容或多行文本、URL、代码围栏、纯舞台指示和超长文本的快速拒绝路径。
使用 Unicode scalar 计数模拟 Python 字符串长度，并按 Unicode scalar 截断对话上下文、原因和错误文本。
构建与源实现一致的中文系统提示词和用户提示词，最近对话最多保留 1200 个 Unicode scalar。
解析原始 JSON、JSON 代码围栏及包含嵌入 JSON 对象的模型响应。
兼容布尔值、数字和常见字符串形式的 sendVoice，并将 confidence 限制在 0 到 1 的范围内。
当模型建议发送语音但置信度低于 0.55 时，强制改为不发送语音。
区分快速拒绝、模型决策和模型调用或解析异常；发生异常时默认不发送语音。
通过 @Sendable 异步闭包接入现有 LLM gateway，避免耦合到具体模型、网络客户端或供应商 SDK。
提供 README，说明行为约定、API 用法、错误语义和集成边界。

modules.summary: Continues the existing LLMRouting subsystem and preserves its routing implementation while extending it into a reusable Swift responsibility cluster. Includes dependency-injected task routing, chat/moments/TTS slot fallbacks, masked-key diagnostics, model cost estimation, persistent usage telemetry, routing diagnostics, and a gateway compatibility façade. The design keeps HTTP transport, provider request execution, and Anthropic-specific request handling delegated to the existing LLMTransport, LLMGateway, and AnthropicMessages components rather than duplicating them. The current project was inspected read-only: the existing LLMRouting module contained LLMRouting.swift and README.md, and the adjacent gateway and transport public interfaces were reviewed. No tests, builds, or git operations were run.
capabilities: Resolves task keys while preserving the source behavior for has_ui_slot=false, provider ID/name matching, model overrides, and chat-slot fallback.
Supports chat configuration with provider/profile selection and the default deepseek profile.
Supports moments, comments, vision, selector, and private slots with per-slot profile/model overrides and chat fallback.
Supports TTS extract and annotate slots, nested configuration sections, legacy top-level configuration, and chat fallback.
Loads route JSON defensively and preserves unknown profile metadata through a Codable JSON value type.
Reports missing or visibly masked API keys without printing or embedding credential values in diagnostics.
Estimates cost using ordered, case-insensitive model substring pricing and source-compatible token coercion.
Records per-task and per-day token usage, cost, latency, success/failure counts, and cache statistics using an actor-isolated telemetry store.
Persists usage JSON atomically and tolerates absent or malformed prior usage data.
Exposes routing diagnostics without making HTTP requests.
Provides compatibility closures for existing gateway entry points without reimplementing LLMGateway or LLMTransport.
Documents source mapping, integration boundaries, dependency injection, telemetry schema, and operational limitations.

modules.summary: Continues the existing KaomojiStore subsystem without changing scope. The current output directory was inspected, and the module files from the previous artifact were not present there, so this response returns the complete self-contained artifact again. The implementation covers the source module's path resolution, normalization, defensive loading, legacy migration, and persistence. It also exposes a public normalization entry point for arbitrary JSON data, uses Unicode-scalar truncation, and improves Python-style conversion of JSON-compatible values. No tests, builds, or git operations were run.
capabilities: Resolves and creates the source-compatible Stickers/kaomoji directory beneath an injected saves root.
Resolves the primary store.json path and provides a reusable actor-isolated filesystem service.
Provides Codable, Equatable, Sendable models for the store and its categories.
Normalizes root data to categories, favorites, recent, and activePack while dropping unknown root fields.
Enforces the source collection limits: 40 categories, 80 items per category, 80 favorites, and 48 recent entries.
Trims strings, limits category names to 32 Unicode scalars and other strings to 64 Unicode scalars, removes empty list items, and deduplicates lists while preserving order.
Applies list limits before filtering, matching Python slicing behavior.
Approximates Python truthiness and string conversion for JSON-compatible values, including null, booleans, numbers, arrays, and objects.
Provides public normalization from JSON Data as well as normalization of typed store values.
Loads a valid primary store and otherwise attempts legacy category migration or returns defaults.
Supports legacy custom files containing either a root category array or an object with a categories array.
Attempts to migrate an existing malformed legacy file using defaults, saves the normalized store, and best-effort renames the legacy file with a .migrated suffix.
Suppresses load and migration failures where the Python source does so, while typed save APIs report directory, encoding, and write failures.
Writes pretty-printed UTF-8 JSON atomically without escaping forward slashes.
Injects the saves root, optional legacy file URL, and FileManager without hardcoded application paths.
Documents the source mapping, public API, normalization limits, migration behavior, concurrency model, usage, and compatibility limitations.

modules.summary: Ports the complete backend sticker-catalog service into reusable native Swift. Preserves the Python implementation's catalog loading behavior, insertion-order-independent final sorting, path traversal rejection, metadata fallback semantics, prompt formatting, and exact-ID, suffix, and filename-based identifier resolution. Provides typed catalog models, configurable filesystem roots, injectable file access, Foundation-only JSON parsing, and an aggregate service API. No frontend functionality, tests, builds, or Git operations are included.
capabilities: Loads descriptions.json from an injected sticker-assets directory and returns an empty catalog when the file is missing, unreadable, or contains invalid JSON.
Accepts only dictionary-shaped catalog roots and dictionary-shaped metadata entries, skipping invalid entries without failing the entire catalog.
Rejects empty identifiers and identifiers containing a path component exactly equal to .., while preserving the source's slash normalization, whitespace trimming, and leading-slash removal behavior.
Normalizes backslashes to forward slashes and confines accepted relative identifiers through source-compatible validation.
Produces catalog entries with id, path, file, collection, description, and URL fields, preserving metadata fallback behavior and the /assets/Stickers/ URL prefix.
Sorts catalog entries by collection and then filename using deterministic Swift string ordering.
Generates prompt-ready sticker lists using the original '- id：description' format, newline separators, and configurable maximum item count.
Normalizes requested sticker identifiers by trying exact IDs first, then path-suffix matches, then exact filename matches, preserving catalog iteration order for ambiguous matches.
Exposes strongly typed StickerCatalogEntry, StickerCatalogConfiguration, StickerCatalogError, and StickerCatalogService APIs.
Supports dependency injection for filesystem access and asset-root configuration without hardcoding project-specific absolute paths.
Provides asynchronous actor-isolated service operations and a synchronous prompt formatter for integration with downstream prompt construction.
Documents source mapping, public contracts, configuration, compatibility details, path-safety limitations, and usage.

modules.summary: Created and read-back-verified a standalone native Swift search-provider subsystem with injected HTTP transport, Serper/Wikipedia/DuckDuckGo fallback, Xiaohongshu REST search, routing heuristics, result deduplication, prompt formatting, login status, and image-candidate selection. Added URL validation, configurable timeouts, bounded accepted response sizes, and upstream research and license documentation. No tests, builds, or Git operations were run.
capabilities: Preserves auto, xiaohongshu, web, and both search modes with source-compatible bias inference and provider ordering.
Implements optional Serper, Chinese/English Wikipedia, DuckDuckGo Instant Answer, and DuckDuckGo Lite fallbacks.
Normalizes Xiaohongshu feed results, checks MCP health and login status, and extracts image candidates while preferring image notes over videos.
Provides dependency-injected asynchronous HTTP transport, typed results and errors, configurable timeouts, and response-size limits.
Rejects unsafe Xiaohongshu base URL configurations, including remote cleartext HTTP and URLs containing userinfo, queries, or fragments.
Documents source mapping, public APIs, fallback behavior, limitations, upstream references, and license decisions.
